question: The Recovery and Resilience Facility, created in response to the crisis caused by the COVID19 pandemic, is coming to an end. In accordance with the applicable regulation, Member States must have completed all reforms and investments set out in their national plans by 31 August 2026. The last payment requests can be submitted until 30 September, with payments to be made before 31 December 2026.

According to the Commission’s scoreboard, France has received around EUR 34 billion of the EUR 40 billion planned and is meeting 83% of the milestones and targets set. As a result, nearly EUR 6 billion remains to be disbursed with just a few days until the deadline.

Against the backdrop of a particularly dire budgetary situation, it is essential to be aware of any potential failures on the part of the French government and the financial consequences those failures might entail. Can the Commission state: 1.
the exact amount still to be paid to France and the part likely to be definitively lost?
the milestones, targets, reforms or investments that have not yet been achieved?
the French projects concerned and the reasons which might lead the Commission to suspend or refuse all or part of the last payments?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2026) France submitted its fifth and final payment request on 26 June 2026 under the Recovery and Resilience Facility. On 29 September 2026, the Commission adopted its positive preliminary assessment of France's fifth payment request worth EUR 6.1 billion1.

The Commission has now sent its preliminary assessment to the Economic and Financial Committee (EFC), which has four weeks to deliver its opinion. The payment to France can take place following the EFC's opinion, and the adoption of a payment decision by the Commission later.

Once the payment is made, 100% of the funding allocated to France under its Recovery and Resilience Plan will be delivered, bringing the total amount disbursed to EUR 40.3 billion, with all 176 milestones and targets successfully fulfilled.
1 Commission greenlights France's final payment request of EUR 6.1 billion under NextGenerationEU
